query: How should correlations among material intensities and embodied factors be specified and justified for Monte Carlo uncertainty (e.g., lognormal, triangular, covariance estimates)?

response.query: How should correlations among material intensities and embodied factors be specified and justified for Monte Carlo uncertainty (e.g., lognormal, triangular, covariance estimates)?
response.answer: Use lognormal or triangular distributions for material intensities and embodied factors, with covariance estimates to specify correlations, ensuring justified uncertainty in Monte Carlo simulations.

results.title: The Econometric Approach to Efficiency Analysis
results.content: This chapter provides an overview of techniques for econometric analysis of technical (production) and economic (cost) efficiency.
